title: Osteoporosis risque évaluation Instrument (ORAI)
formula:
The ORAI is calculated by adding the selected points for each variable:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Age, years | 45-54 | 0 |
| 55-64 | 5 | |
| 65-74 | 9 | |
| ≥75 | 15 | |
| Weight | >69 kg (>152.1 lbs) | 0 |
| 60-69 kg (132.3-152.1 lbs) | 3 | |
| <60 kg (<132.3 lbs) | 9 | |
| Current estrogen use | Yes | 0 |
| No | 2 | |

how_to_use.why:
- In contrast to other tools that calculate fracture risk, this tool was specifically created to predict who is at risk of low BMD, aiding in the decision-making for additional screening.
- Enables targeted BMD screening, potentially reducing the necessity for all women to undergo bone densitometry testing.
how_to_use.when:
- Can be used during routine health visits to determine the appropriateness of osteoporosis screening in women.
- Particularly beneficial for women under 65 years of age, as clinical guidelines often base the recommendation for bone mineral density (BMD) testing on clinical risk factors.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Not intended for use in patients at high-risk for osteoporosis due to secondary causes (e.g., chronic corticosteroid therapy, primary hyperparathyroidism).
- Results are not diagnostic for osteoporosis and do not replace bone densitometry.
- Does not offer recommendations for subsequent bone densitometry testing or for monitoring the efficacy of osteoporosis treatment.

next_steps.management:
- A score of 9 or higher suggests a high risk for osteoporosis, warranting further investigation through bone densitometry screening.
- While the ORAI provides guidance on which patients may require additional screening, it does not account for all potential risk factors for osteoporosis. Therefore, clinical judgment is crucial in determining the appropriate next steps for each patient.

more_info:
Interpretation:

| ORAI Score | Bone Densitometry |
| --- | --- |
| <9 | Bone densitometry may not be needed in this patient. |
| ≥9 | Bone densitometry should be considered for this patient. |
